discovery: Development of silicon microstrip and hybrid pixel detectors for precision particle tracking and imaging

nominees.name: Josef Kemmer
nominees.affiliation: Technical University of Munich (emeritus); founder of Ketek GmbH, Germany

motivation: Kemmer's planar process (1980) made fully depleted, low-leakage silicon strip sensors manufacturable with semiconductor-industry techniques. Heijne led the first use of silicon microstrip detectors in high-energy experiments and, with Parker, pioneered hybrid pixel detectors in which sensors are bump-bonded to CMOS readout. Parker also invented 3D silicon sensors, which are radiation-hard. These devices resolve secondary vertices at the micron level. That made b-tagging possible, which was decisive for the top-quark discovery at the Tevatron and the Higgs observation at the LHC, and it underlies heavy-flavour physics at LEP, the B-factories and LHCb. Hybrid pixel technology also led to single-photon-counting imagers (Medipix/Timepix) that are now used in synchrotron science, medical CT and space dosimetry. Silicon tracking is the backbone of every modern collider detector. It is a true instrumentation breakthrough that made new physics measurable.
